The statement is true. Write c(m) = 3 if m ≡ 2 (mod 4) and c(m) = −1 otherwise, so the series is Σ c(m)·log m / m. Its Dirichlet series is F(s) = Σ c(m) m^(−s) = −(1 − 2^(1−s))² ζ(s). Since F(1) = 0, the sum equals −F′(1) = log²2, which matches `putnam_2017_b4_solution`. The series is absolutely summable in the grouped form (the block terms are O(log k / k²)), so `tsum` is not trivially 0.

A Lean proof would need to pass from the Dirichlet series to its value and derivative at s = 1, either through analytic continuation or an Abel-type limit argument with uniform convergence, plus the asymptotics of the block sums. That is far more formalization than I can finish here, and I can't test intermediate steps against Mathlib sources. I'm stopping rather than submitting an incomplete proof.
